learningObjective: Trace how two successes and one failure update an illustrative Beta(1,1) prior to Beta(3,2), changing its mean from 0.50 to 0.60 without eliminating uncertainty or authorizing ineligible exploration.
mediumRationale: An original density plot directly shows the stated mathematical prior and posterior. The exact cubic represents 12*p^2*(1-p), not measured recommendation weights or a universal personalization schedule.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a flowchart can show the feedback loop, but its node layout would make the changing relative roles of fallback and behavioral signals less direct and would add a runtime dependency.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: overlay the normalized uniform prior and exact Beta(3,2) density, label the posterior mean and distinguish curves by line style. Both distributions are explicitly illustrative under stable independent Bernoulli reward assumptions.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: The earlier two-stage handoff card described signal families but did not draw the new numerical uncertainty update. Prose and the decision contract now carry that operational context.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: an adjustable session count would require invented weight values and state without adding a more defensible lesson than the staged trace.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the reviewed sources establish cold-start and feedback mechanisms but no source figure narrowly expresses this article's staged signal handoff; figure-reuse permission was not assumed.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the posterior mean alone hides the uncertainty that remains after three mature observations. The density overlay makes that distinction inspectable without inventing a production transition threshold.

pages.insight: The preceding slide is about model compression, establishing the boundary before the recommender-system section and adding no cold-start mechanism.
This is the recommender-systems section divider; it introduces the relevant neighborhood but contains no explanatory figure or cold-start guidance.

The collaborative-filtering slide says interaction-only matrix factorization needs user fold-in, notes presentation-bias feedback and explore/exploit, suggests average ratings as a new user's initial ratings, and recommends user, item, and context features when available.

The adjacent content-based and hybrid-recommender slide explains item-attribute similarity and linear blending of content-based and collaborative outputs, but does not show how their influence should change as a new user generates behavior.
The next slide begins a personalized-search case study, marking the end of the local recommender-method sequence.

The search case study later separates general context and trending items from past behavior and personalized context at ranking time, reinforcing the distinct signal families without describing a new-user transition.
The ML-design overview asks how fresh data and cold starts affect sampling and model design, but offers no mechanism for blending signals.
The production checklist explicitly asks for strategies for new customers and explore/exploit adaptation, confirming these as deployment concerns rather than supplying a spatial explanation.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for cold start, new user, recommender, collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, hybrid, explore/exploit, and personalization. All matching pages were read; pages 128-132 were inspected as the core neighborhood, with later supporting matches on pages 135, 161, and 162. Page 29 mentions recommender sparsity only as an example for factorization machines and does not apply to the user-lifetime handoff. No deck image, wording, values, or layout is copied.

sourceReview.notes: Historical source review for the earlier semantic handoff card: cold-start is not a hard switch after a fixed interaction count; permitted onboarding, context, content and population evidence can precede behavior. The current independently authored Beta density is a mathematical teaching example, not a result or figure from these sources. The recorded source and agent reviews are historical provenance, not a fresh cross-review of this SVG.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, searched all 214 deck pages and inspected the recommender neighborhood and later cold-start references, then checked a primary cold-start paper, a primary contextual-bandit paper, and official content-based and collaborative-filtering documentation before selecting an original semantic handoff card.

implementation.accessibility: The figure and SVG have linked titles; the SVG has a linked description and a direct reading caption. Dashed prior and solid posterior curves, named distributions, axes and the mean label do not depend on color. A 400-pixel minimum canvas sits in the existing horizontal scroller. The exact cubic, normalization, mean, mode and update passed local arithmetic checks; native theme, scroll-endpoint and print qualification remain separate requirements.
